facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic, 200–190 million years ago.

facts.statement: The species Heterodontosaurus tucki was named in 1962 based on a skull found in South Africa.
facts.quote: Its only known member species, Heterodontosaurus tucki, was named in 1962 based on a skull discovered in South Africa.

facts.statement: An almost complete skeleton of Heterodontosaurus was discovered in 1966.
facts.quote: Further specimens have since been found, including an almost complete skeleton in 1966.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was a small dinosaur that grew between 1.18 and 1.75 meters long and weighed between 2 and 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Though it was a small dinosaur, Heterodontosaurus was one of the largest members of its family, reaching between 1.18 m and possibly 1.75 m in length, and weighing between 2 and 10 kg.

facts.statement: The front of the jaws of Heterodontosaurus was covered by a horny beak.
facts.quote: The front of the jaws were covered in a horny beak.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had three types of teeth, including small incisor-like teeth and long canine-like tusks in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: It had three types of teeth; in the upper jaw, small, incisor-like teeth were followed by long, canine-like tusks.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a short body and a long tail.
facts.quote: The body was short with a long tail.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had long, robust five-fingered forelimbs and long, slender hindlimbs with four toes.
facts.quote: The five-fingered forelimbs were long and relatively robust, whereas the hind-limbs were long, slender, and had four toes.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Heterodontosaurus tucki was discovered during a British–South African expedition in 1961–1962.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Heterodontosaurus tucki (SAM-PK-K337) was discovered during the British–South African expedition to South Africa and Basutoland (former name of Lesotho) in 1961–1962.

facts.statement: The holotype was excavated at the Tyinindini locality in the Cape Province of South Africa at an altitude of about 1890 meters.
facts.quote: It was excavated on a mountain at an altitude of about 1890 m, at a locality called Tyinindini, in the district of Transkei (sometimes referred to as Herschel) in the Cape Province of South Africa.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was scientifically described and named in 1962 by Alfred Walter Crompton and Alan J. Charig.
facts.quote: The animal was scientifically described and named in 1962 by palaeontologists Alfred Walter Crompton and Alan J. Charig.

facts.statement: A second specimen was discovered in 1966 at the Voyizane locality in the Elliot Formation of the Stormberg Group, 1,770 meters above sea level.
facts.quote: In 1966, a second specimen of Heterodontosaurus (SAM-PK-K1332) was discovered at the Voyizane locality, in the Elliot Formation of the Stormberg Group of rock formations, 1,770 m above sea level, on Krommespruit Mountain.

facts.statement: The second specimen included the skull and skeleton preserved in articulation with little displacement or distortion.
facts.quote: This specimen included both the skull and skeleton, preserved in articulation (i.e. the bones being preserved in their natural position in relation to each other), with little displacement and distortion of the bones.

facts.statement: The postcranial skeleton of the second specimen was briefly described in 1976 by Albert Santa Luca, Crompton, and Charig.
facts.quote: The postcranial skeleton was briefly described by palaeontologists Albert Santa Luca, Crompton and Charig in 1976.

facts.statement: The skeleton of the second specimen was fully described in 1980.
facts.quote: The skeleton was fully described in 1980.

facts.statement: The skull of Heterodontosaurus was fully described in 2011 by David B. Norman and colleagues.
facts.quote: It was not until 2011 that the skull was fully described by the palaeontologist David B. Norman and colleagues.

facts.statement: A partial snout found in 1975 was originally thought to belong to Massospondylus but was reclassified as Heterodontosaurus in 2011.
facts.quote: A partial snout (NM QR 1788) found in 1975 on Tushielaw Farm south of Voyizane was thought to belong to Massospondylus until 2011, when it was reclassified as Heterodontosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1970, Richard A. Thulborn suggested that Heterodontosaurus was a junior synonym of the genus Lycorhinus.
facts.quote: In 1970, palaeontologist Richard A. Thulborn suggested that Heterodontosaurus was a junior synonym of the genus Lycorhinus, which was named in 1924 with the species L. angustidens, also from a specimen discovered in South Africa.

facts.statement: Thulborn reclassified the type species as Lycorhinus tucki, arguing for distinctness based on tooth differences and stratigraphy.
facts.quote: He reclassified the type species as a member of the older genus, as the new combination Lycorhinus tucki, which he considered distinct due to slight differences in its teeth and its stratigraphy.

facts.statement: In 1974, Charig and Crompton agreed Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus belonged to the same family but disagreed on whether they were similar enough to be in the same genus.
facts.quote: In 1974, Charig and Crompton agreed that Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus belonged in the same family, Heterodontosauridae, but disagreed that they were similar enough to be considered congeneric.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is now thought to have been bipedal, whereas it was formerly believed to be capable of quadrupedal locomotion.
facts.quote: Though it was formerly thought to have been capable of quadrupedal locomotion, it is now thought to have been bipedal.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus exhibited sporadic tooth replacement rather than continuous replacement, unlike its relatives.
facts.quote: Tooth replacement was sporadic and not continuous, unlike its relatives.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is the namesake and best-known member of the family Heterodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is the eponymous and best-known member of the family Heterodontosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus name Heterodontosaurus means "different toothed lizard", referring to its unusual heterodont dentition.
facts.quote: the genus name means "different toothed lizard", in reference to its unusual, heterodont dentition

facts.statement: The specific name tucki honors G. C. Tuck, who supported the discoverers.
facts.quote: the specific name honours G. C. Tuck, who supported the discoverers.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was a small dinosaur.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus was a small dinosaur.

facts.statement: The most complete skeleton of Heterodontosaurus measured approximately 1.18 meters in length.
facts.quote: The most complete skeleton, SAM-PK-K1332, belonged to an animal measuring about 1.18 m in length.

facts.statement: Studies have estimated the weight of Heterodontosaurus at 1.8 kg, 2.59 kg, and 3.4 kg.
facts.quote: Its weight was variously estimated at 1.8 kg, 2.59 kg, and 3.4 kg in separate studies.

facts.statement: An incomplete skull specimen suggests Heterodontosaurus could have reached a length of 1.75 meters and a mass of nearly 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: A second specimen, consisting of an incomplete skull, indicates that Heterodontosaurus could have grown substantially larger – up to a length of 1.75 m and with a body mass of nearly 10 kg.

facts.statement: The size of Heterodontosaurus has been compared to that of a turkey.
facts.quote: The size of this dinosaur has been compared to that of a turkey.

facts.statement: Following the discovery of filamentous integuments on Tianyulong in 2009, Heterodontosaurus has been depicted with similar structures in publications by Gregory S. Paul and Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: Following the description of the related Tianyulong in 2009, which was preserved with hundreds of long, filamentous integuments (sometimes compared to bristles) from neck to tail, Heterodontosaurus has also been depicted with such structures, for example in publications by the palaeontologists Gregory S. Paul and Paul Sereno.

facts.statement: A restoration by Paul Sereno included a hypothetical display structure on the snout above the nasal fossa.
facts.quote: The restoration published by Sereno also featured a hypothetical display structure located on the snout, above the nasal fossa (depression).

facts.statement: The two most complete skulls of Heterodontosaurus measured 108 mm and 121 mm in length.
facts.quote: The two most complete skulls measured 108 mm (holotype specimen SAM-PK-K337) and 121 mm (specimen SAM-PK-K1332) in length.

facts.statement: The skull of Heterodontosaurus was elongated, narrow, and triangular, sloping down from the sagittal crest to the snout tip.
facts.quote: The skull was elongated, narrow, and triangular when viewed from the side, with the highest point being the sagittal crest, from where the skull sloped down towards the snout tip.

facts.statement: The back of the Heterodontosaurus skull ended in a hook-like shape offset to the quadrate bone.
facts.quote: The back of the skull ended in a hook-like shape, which was offset to the quadrate bone.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a large, circular eye opening with a spur-like bone protruding into the upper part of the orbit.
facts.quote: The orbit (eye opening) was large and circular, and a large spur-like bone, the palpebral, protruded backwards into the upper part of the opening.

facts.statement: A horn-like structure projected sideways from the jugal bone below the eye socket in Heterodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Below the eye socket, the jugal bone gave rise to a sideways projecting boss, or horn-like structure.

facts.statement: The front of the jaws in Heterodontosaurus was covered by a toothless keratinous beak.
facts.quote: The front of the jaws were covered by a toothless keratinous beak (or rhamphotheca).

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus possessed different-shaped teeth, a feature known as heterodonty that is mainly associated with mammals.
facts.quote: An unusual feature of the skull was the different-shaped teeth (heterodonty) for which the genus is named, which is otherwise mainly known from mammals.

facts.statement: Unlike most dinosaurs and reptiles, Heterodontosaurus had three different types of teeth.
facts.quote: Most dinosaurs (and indeed most reptiles) have a single type of tooth in their jaws, but Heterodontosaurus had three.

facts.statement: The first two upper teeth of Heterodontosaurus were small and cone-shaped, while the third formed prominent, canine-like tusks.
facts.quote: The first two upper teeth were small and cone-shaped (comparable to incisors), while the third on each side was much enlarged, forming prominent, canine-like tusks.

facts.statement: The canine teeth of Heterodontosaurus had fine serrations along the back edge, with only the lower ones serrated at the front.
facts.quote: The canines had fine serrations along the back edge, but only the lower ones were serrated at the front.

facts.statement: The inset upper and lower teeth rows of Heterodontosaurus created a cheek-recess also found in other ornithischians.
facts.quote: The upper and lower teeth rows were inset, which created a "cheek-recess" also seen in other ornithischians.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the size difference between Heterodontosaurus specimens reflects variability within a species, sexual dimorphism, or the existence of two separate species.
facts.quote: The reason for the size difference between the two specimens is unclear, and might reflect variability within a single species, sexual dimorphism, or the presence of two separate species.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that basal ornithischians like Heterodontosaurus may have had lip-like structures similar to lizards rather than bridging skin between the jaws.
facts.quote: It has also been suggested that heterodontosaurs and other basal (or "primitive") orhithischians had lip-like structures like lizards do (based on similarities in their jaws), rather than bridging skin between the upper and lower jaws (such as cheeks).

facts.statement: The trunk of Heterodontosaurus was short, containing 12 dorsal vertebrae and 6 fused sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: The trunk was short, consisting of 12 dorsal and 6 fused sacral vertebrae.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a long tail estimated to contain between 34 and 37 vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail was long compared to the body; although incompletely known, it probably consisted of 34 to 37 caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons stiffened the dorsal spine of Heterodontosaurus starting from the fourth vertebra.
facts.quote: The dorsal spine was stiffened by ossified tendons, beginning with the fourth dorsal vertebra.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus possessed a suprascapula capping the shoulder blade, a feature otherwise known only in the dinosaur Parksosaurus.
facts.quote: The shoulder blade was capped by an additional element, the suprascapula, which is, among dinosaurs, otherwise only known from Parksosaurus.

facts.statement: The gastralia of Heterodontosaurus were arranged in two lengthwise rows, each with about nine elements.
facts.quote: The gastralia were arranged in two lengthwise rows, each containing around nine elements.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Heterodontosaurus were robust and measured 70% of the length of the hind limbs.
facts.quote: The forelimbs were robustly built and proportionally long, measuring 70% of the length of the hind limbs.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a large hand nearly as long as the humerus, equipped with five grasping fingers.
facts.quote: The hand was large, approaching the humerus in length, and possessed five fingers equipped for grasping.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula of the hand in Heterodontosaurus was 2-3-4-3-2.
facts.quote: The phalangeal formula, which states the number of finger bones in each finger starting from the first, was 2-3-4-3-2.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had long, slender hindlimbs ending in four toes, with the first toe (hallux) not touching the ground.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs were long, slender, and ended in four toes, the first of which (the hallux) did not contact the ground.

facts.statement: The tibiotarsus of Heterodontosaurus was approximately 30% longer than the femur.
facts.quote: The tibiotarsus was about 30% longer than the femur.

facts.statement: The toe bones of Heterodontosaurus ended in claw-like unguals rather than the hoof-like structures found in more advanced ornithischians.
facts.quote: The ungual bones of the toes were claw-like, and not hoof-like as in more advanced ornithischians.

facts.statement: Palaeontologists Alfred Romer and Oskar Kuhn independently named the family Heterodontosauridae in 1966 to include Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus.
facts.quote: The palaeontologists Alfred Romer and Oskar Kuhn independently named the family Heterodontosauridae in 1966 as a family of ornithischian dinosaurs including Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurids lived from the Late Triassic to the Early Cretaceous, existing for at least 100 million years.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurids persisted from the Late Triassic until the Early Cretaceous period, and existed for at least a 100 million years.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurids are known from Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, though most fossils come from southern Africa.
facts.quote: They are known from Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, but the majority have been found in southern Africa.

facts.statement: Some scientists dispute that Heterodontosaurus's hand pattern indicates a primitive relationship with saurischians, suggesting instead that similarities arose from convergent evolution.
facts.quote: This was disputed by some scientists who believed the two groups had instead evolved independently from "thecodontian" archosaur ancestors, and that their similarities were due to convergent evolution.

facts.statement: In 2017, Matthew G. Baron and colleagues suggested grouping ornithischians with theropods in the clade Ornithoscelida based on similarities between Heterodontosaurus and Eoraptor.
facts.quote: In 2017, similarities between the skeletons of Heterodontosaurus and the early theropod Eoraptor were used by palaeontologist Matthew G. Baron and colleagues to suggest that ornithischians should be grouped with theropods in a group called Ornithoscelida.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is commonly considered a herbivorous dinosaur.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is commonly regarded as a herbivorous dinosaur.

facts.statement: In 1974, Thulborn suggested that the tusks were used for combat, display, or defense rather than feeding.
facts.quote: In 1974, Thulborn proposed that the tusks of the dinosaur played no important role in feeding; rather, that they would have been used in combat with conspecifics, for display, as a visual threat, or for active defence.

facts.statement: In 2000, Paul Barrett proposed that Heterodontosaurus may have been an occasional carnivore based on tooth and tusk serration.
facts.quote: In 2000, Paul Barrett suggested that the shape of the premaxillary teeth and the fine serration of the tusks are reminiscent of carnivorous animals, hinting at facultative carnivory.

facts.statement: In 2008, Butler and colleagues argued that enlarged tusks were not a sign of sexual dimorphism because they developed early in life.
facts.quote: In 2008, Butler and colleagues argued that the enlarged tusks formed early in the development of the individual, and therefore could not constitute sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: In 2011, Norman and colleagues noted that Heterodontosaurus had long arms with large, curved claws capable of seizing small prey.
facts.quote: In 2011, Norman and colleagues drew attention to the arms and hands, which are relatively long and equipped with large, recurved claws.

facts.statement: In 2012, Sereno argued that skull and dentition features indicate a diet that was purely or mostly herbivorous.
facts.quote: In 2012, Sereno pointed out several skull and dentition features that suggest a purely or at least preponderantly herbivorous diet.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had enlarged jaw muscles and a jaw joint positioned below the teeth.
facts.quote: The jaw muscles were enlarged, and the jaw joint was set below the level of the teeth.

facts.statement: A 2016 study found that the bite force of Heterodontosaurus was comparable to that of Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2016 study of ornithischian jaw mechanics found that the relative bite forces of Heterodontosaurus was comparable to that of the more derived Scelidosaurus.

facts.statement: There is significant controversy regarding whether Heterodontosaurus exhibited continuous tooth replacement like other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Much controversy has surrounded the question of whether or not, and to what degree, Heterodontosaurus showed the continuous tooth replacement that is typical for other dinosaurs and reptiles.

facts.statement: In 1980, Hopson challenged Thulborn's conclusions about tooth replacement and jaw movement.
facts.quote: A comprehensive analysis conducted in 1980 by Hopson questioned Thulborn's ideas.

facts.statement: Hopson demonstrated that tooth wear patterns indicated vertical and lateral jaw movements instead of back-and-forth movements.
facts.quote: Hopson showed that the wear facet patterns on the teeth in fact indicate vertical and lateral rather than back and forth jaw movements.

facts.statement: Hopson argued that variable tooth wear indicated continuous tooth replacement.
facts.quote: Hopson demonstrated variability in the degree of tooth wear, indicating continuous tooth replacement.

facts.statement: Hopson rejected Thulborn's hypothesis that tooth replacement occurred during aestivation due to a lack of evidence.
facts.quote: Thulborn's aestivation hypothesis was rejected by Hopson due to lack of evidence.

facts.statement: In 2006, Butler and colleagues used CT scans on juvenile skull SAM-PK-K10487 to study tooth replacement.
facts.quote: In 2006, Butler and colleagues conducted computer tomography scans of the juvenile skull SAM-PK-K10487.

facts.statement: Unerupted replacement teeth were first discovered in 2011 in specimen SAM-PK-K1334 described by Norman and colleagues.
facts.quote: Unerupted replacement teeth in Heterodontosaurus were not discovered until 2011, when Norman and colleagues described the upper jaw of specimen SAM-PK-K1334.

facts.statement: A juvenile skull AMNH 24000 described by Sereno in 2012 also contained unerupted replacement teeth.
facts.quote: Another juvenile skull (AMNH 24000) described by Sereno in 2012 also yielded unerupted replacement teeth.

facts.statement: The unerupted replacement teeth in Heterodontosaurus are triangular in lateral view, typical of basal ornithischians.
facts.quote: The unerupted teeth are triangular in lateral view, which is the typical tooth morphology in basal ornithischians.

facts.statement: The genus Heterodontosaurus was established by Charning and Crompton in 1962.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Charning & Crompton 1962

facts.statement: The species H. tucki was described by Charning and Crompton in 1962.
facts.quote: species_authority: Charning & Crompton 1962

facts.statement: Lycorhinus tucki, described by Thulborn in 1970, is a synonym of Heterodontosaurus tucki.
facts.quote: synonyms: Lycorhinus tucki Thulborn, 1970

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Inferior

facts.statement: Alan Charing and Alfred Crompton discovered the remains of Heterodontosaurus in a mountainous escarpment in South Africa during the 1960s.
facts.quote: En la década de 1960, los paleontólogos Alan Charning y Alfred Crompton descubrieron en un escarpado montañoso de Sudáfrica los restos de éste pequeño dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Fossils of Heterodontosaurus were found in the Upper Elliot Formation and the Clarence Formation.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en la Formación Elliot Superior y la Formación Clarence.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was a small dinosaur, reaching lengths between 1.20 and possibly 1.75 meters and weighing between 2 and 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Aunque era un dinosaurio pequeño, Heterodontosaurus era uno de los miembros más grandes de su familia, alcanzaba entre 1,20 metros y posiblemente 1,75 metros de longitud y pesaba entre 2 y 10 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had long, relatively robust five-fingered forelimbs and long, thin four-fingered hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores de cinco dedos eran largas y relativamente robustas, mientras que las extremidades posteriores eran largas, delgadas y tenían cuatro dedos.

facts.statement: The skull of Heterodontosaurus was elongated, narrow, and triangular when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: El cráneo era alargado, estrecho y triangular cuando se veía desde el lado.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had three types of teeth in its upper jaw: small incisor-like teeth, followed by long canine-like fangs, separated from chisel-shaped teeth by a gap.
facts.quote: Tenía tres tipos de dientes, en la mandíbula superior, los dientes pequeños, como incisivos, seguidos por largos colmillos, como caninos. Una brecha dividía los colmillos de los dientes con forma de cincel.

facts.statement: While previously thought to be quadrupedal, Heterodontosaurus is now believed to have been bipedal.
facts.quote: Aunque antes se pensaba que era capaz de una locomoción cuadrúpeda, ahora se cree que fue bípedo.

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives, Heterodontosaurus had sporadic rather than continuous tooth replacement.
facts.quote: El reemplazo dental fue esporádico y no continuo, a diferencia de sus parientes.

facts.statement: The most complete skeleton of Heterodontosaurus, specimen SAM-PK-K1332, belonged to an animal measuring approximately 1.18 meters in length.
facts.quote: El esqueleto más completo, SAM-PK-K1332, pertenecía a un animal que medía aproximadamente 1.18 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The weight of the most complete Heterodontosaurus specimen has been estimated to vary between 1.8, 2.59, and 3.4 kilograms in separate studies.
facts.quote: Su peso se estimó de manera diversa variando entre 1,8 kilogramos, 2,59 kilogramos y 3.4 kilogramos en estudios separados.

facts.statement: A second, incomplete skull specimen suggests Heterodontosaurus could have grown up to 1.75 meters in length and nearly 10 kilograms in mass.
facts.quote: Un segundo espécimen, que consiste en un cráneo incompleto, indica que Heterodontosaurus podría haber crecido sustancialmente más grande, hasta una longitud de 1,75 m y con una masa corporal de casi 10 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus teeth came in three shapes: small and sharp, long and curved canine-like teeth possibly present only in males, and molar-like teeth.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Heterodontosaurus presentaban tres formas diferentes, los pequeños y afilados, los largos y curvos caniniformes, posiblemente sólo presentes en los machos y los molariformes o molares.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a beak at the front of its jaw and small teeth behind it likely used for cutting leaves and shoots.
facts.quote: En el frente de la mandíbula tenía un pico y detrás pequeños dientes usados probablemente para cortar hojas y brotes.

facts.statement: The fused ankle structure of Heterodontosaurus resembles that of birds.
facts.quote: La estructura fusionada del tobillo hace recordar a la de las aves.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had tiny wrist bones, making the wrist functional and versatile, possibly used for grasping and pulling leaves.
facts.quote: Los huesos de sus muñecas eran diminutos, de ahí que la muñeca fuera funcional y versátil. Esta podría haber servido para agarrar y arrancar hojas.

facts.statement: The neck of Heterodontosaurus consisted of 9 cervical vertebrae that likely formed an S-curve.
facts.quote: El cuello consistía en 9 vértebras cervicales , que habrían formado una curva en forma de S, como lo indica la forma de los cuerpos vertebrales en la vista lateral del esqueleto.

facts.statement: The spine of Heterodontosaurus was rigidified by ossified tendons starting from the fourth dorsal vertebra, a feature likely helping to counteract stress during bipedal locomotion.
facts.quote: La espina dorsal estaba rígida por tendones osificados, comenzando por la cuarta vértebra dorsal. Esta característica está presente en muchos otros dinosaurios ornitisquios y probablemente contrarrestó el estrés causado por las fuerzas de flexión que actúan sobre la columna vertebral durante la locomoción bípeda.

facts.statement: Unlike many other ornithischians, the tail of Heterodontosaurus lacked ossified tendons and was likely flexible.
facts.quote: En contraste con muchos otros ornitisquios, la cola de Heterodontosaurus carecía de tendones osificados, y por lo tanto era probablemente flexible.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Heterodontosaurus were robust and proportionally long, measuring 70% of the length of the hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores fueron construidas de manera robusta y proporcionalmente largas, midiendo el 70% de la longitud de las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: The hand of Heterodontosaurus was large, nearly as long as the humerus, and had five grasping fingers.
facts.quote: La mano era grande, se acercaba al húmero en longitud y tenía cinco dedos equipados para agarrar.

facts.statement: The first three fingers of Heterodontosaurus ended in large, strong claws, while the fourth and fifth fingers were strongly reduced and possibly vestigial.
facts.quote: Los primeros tres dedos terminaron en garras grandes y fuertes. Los dedos cuarto y quinto fueron fuertemente reducidos, y posiblemente vestigiales.

facts.statement: The hind legs of Heterodontosaurus were long and thin, ending in four toes, the first of which, the hallux, did not touch the ground.
facts.quote: Las patas traseras eran largas, delgadas y terminaban en cuatro dedos, el primero de los cuales, el hallux, no tocaba el suelo.

facts.statement: Unique among ornithischians, several leg and foot bones of Heterodontosaurus were fused, including the tibia and fibula fusing with upper tarsal bones to form a tibiotarsus, and lower tarsal bones fusing with metatarsals to form a tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: Único para un ornitisquio, varios huesos de la pierna y el pie se fusionaron, la tibia y el peroné se fusionaron con los huesos del tarso superior, astrágalo y calcáneo , formando un tibiotarsos, mientras que los huesos del tarso inferior se fusionaron con los huesos metatarsianos, formando un tarsometatarsos.

facts.statement: The ungual bones of the feet of Heterodontosaurus were like claws, not hooves like in more advanced ornithischians.
facts.quote: Los huesos unguales de los dedos de los pies eran como garras, y no como cascos como en oornitisquios más avanzados.

facts.statement: Following the description of Tianyulong in 2009, Heterodontosaurus has also been described as having long, filamentous structures from neck to tail, sometimes compared to quills.
facts.quote: Siguiendo la descripción del relacionado Tianyulong en 2009, que se conservó con cientos de estructuras largas y filamentosas a veces comparadas con cerdas desde el cuello hasta la cola, Heterodontosaurus también se ha descrito con tales estructuras, por ejemplo en publicaciones del paleontólogo estadounidense Gregory S. Paul y Paul Sereno .

facts.statement: Paul Sereno has stated that a living Heterodontosaurus may have looked like an "agile two-legged porcupine."
facts.quote: Sereno ha declarado que un Heterodontosaurus puede haber parecido un " puercoespín ágil de dos patas" en la vida.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus tucki is the only known species of the extinct genus Heterodontosaurus, a heterodontosaurid neornithischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus tucki es la única especie conocida del género extinto Heterodontosaurus (gr. "lagarto de dientes diferentes") de dinosaurio neornitisquio heterodontosáurido

facts.statement: The family Heterodontosauridae is considered one of the most primitive or basal groups within the order of ornithischian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Esta familia es considerada uno de los grupos más primitivos o basales dentro del orden de los dinosaurios ornitisquios .

facts.statement: Many paleontologists still consider Heterodontosaurus an ornithopod, although the theory of classifying it within ceratopsians is increasingly accepted.
facts.quote: Muchos paleontólogos aún consideran al Heterodontosaurus como un ornitópodo, aunque cada vez es más aceptada la teoría de clasificarlo dentro de los ceratopsios.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that heterodontosauriforms may have given rise to marginocephalians, possibly explaining the transitional characteristics of Yinlong.
facts.quote: Se cree también que los heterodontosauriformes pudieron dar origen a los marginocéfalos, lo que posiblemente explicaría las características transicionales del Yinlong.

facts.statement: Based on anatomy and physiology, Heterodontosaurus is considered a ceratopsian and distinct from ornithopods, despite ongoing debate.
facts.quote: Por lo que demuestran ambas teorías, se considera a estos como ceratopsios, puesto que su anatomía y su fisiología corresponden a este grupo y se alejan de los ornitópodos.

facts.statement: The genus Heterodontosaurus was named by Crompton and Charig in 1962.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Heterodontosaurus (genus), Crompton and Charig 1962
